SE3 raises $30 million to expand onboard spatial AI for unmanned systems

SE3 announced a $30 million Series A on November 12, led by Accel with Keen, Lakestar and Seedcamp. The Munich company develops spatial-intelligence software for unmanned systems. Funding will expand engineering, commercial and operations teams and support a UK office.

SE3 ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Capital for European expansion

SE3 announced a $30 million Series A on November 12, led by Accel with Keen, Lakestar and Seedcamp. The Munich company develops spatial-intelligence software for unmanned systems. Funding will expand engineering, commercial and operations teams and support a UK office.

Shared perception across platforms

The company describes software that combines sensor observations from different manufacturers’ drones and ground vehicles into a shared 3D environment. Onboard processing addresses connectivity and satellite-signal limitations. Auterion says the technology runs on Skynode computers. The announcement does not provide independent testing establishing performance in every condition.

Civilian applications are a future direction

SE3 reports thousands of systems shipped over two years and work with Ukraine and Germany’s armed forces, without disclosing contract values or revenue. Defense remains the main market. Civilian robotics and emergency response are areas it plans to explore from 2027, rather than completed civilian deployments.
